text:
📚🧠 EVERY AI COMPANY WANTS TO CHANGE EDUCATION.

But before a child can prompt an AI…

Before they can research.

Before they can study science.

Before they can understand history.

Before they can evaluate whether something online is true.

Before they can learn independently…

They need one foundational ability:

THEY NEED TO READ.

And not merely recognize words.

They need to:

Decode.

Understand.

Question.

Remember.

Connect ideas.

Build vocabulary.

Evaluate information.

And eventually:

LEARN THROUGH READING.

That's the enormous opportunity I see in:

https://t.co/LjouMNFF1E

I wouldn't build another digital bookshelf.

I wouldn't build another AI that summarizes the book so the student doesn't have to read it.

I'd build:

📚✨ THE READING-TO-LEARNING PLATFORM.

One system connecting:

READ → UNDERSTAND → QUESTION → REMEMBER → CONNECT → LEARN

One promise:

READ BETTER. LEARN ANYTHING.™

And the timing is remarkably relevant.

The newest OECD/PISA findings released this month show reading performance among 15-year-olds has fallen sharply internationally, while the OECD is simultaneously emphasizing that reading in the AI era increasingly requires distinguishing fact from opinion, navigating ambiguity and evaluating information critically. (Reuters)

In the U.S., the latest NAEP reading results showed only 31% of fourth-graders at or above NAEP Proficient in 2024. (Nations Report Card)

So the problem isn't:

WE DON'T HAVE ENOUGH CONTENT.

We have more content than any generation in history.

The problem is:

CAN WE ACTUALLY READ IT, UNDERSTAND IT AND LEARN FROM IT?

🔥🔥🔥

📖 READ WITH ME™

This becomes the center of the product.

Open:

A story.

Textbook.

Article.

Historical document.

Science chapter.

Essay.

Research paper.

Then ReadingAndLearning doesn't replace the text.

It sits:

BESIDE THE READER.

Student struggles with a word?

Tap.

Confused by a sentence?

Ask.

Missed an important idea?

Gentle prompt.

Need context?

Explain.

But never turn:

“Help me understand this.”

into:

“Here's a summary so you don't have to read it.”

🔥

🧠 DON'T SKIP THE READING™

This becomes a founding principle.

Student uploads 30 pages and asks:

“Summarize this so I don't have to read it.”

😂

ReadingAndLearning can say:

“I'll help you read it faster and understand it better.”

Then guide them through:

Key sections.

Vocabulary.

Questions.

Connections.

Checks for understanding.

Because the product should optimize for:

LEARNING.

Not:

AVOIDING LEARNING.

🔥🔥🔥

🔤 LEARN TO READ™

For beginning readers, build around established literacy foundations.

The National Reading Panel's framework identifies five major areas:

PHONEMIC AWARENESS

PHONICS

FLUENCY

VOCABULARY

COMPREHENSION (NICHD)

ReadingAndLearning could create individualized pathways across them.

Not:

ONE APP GAME FOR EVERY CHILD.

A real literacy progression.

🔥

👂 SOUND IT OUT™

Child hears:

“ship”

Break it down.

Blend it.

Change a sound.

Match sounds to letters.

Practice.

Celebrate progress.

The system learns which sound-letter relationships need reinforcement.

TEACH THE SKILL.

Don't train the child to guess.

🔥🔥🔥

🔡 PHONICS PATH™

Student knows:

Short vowels ✓

Common consonants ✓

Digraphs ⚠️

Long-vowel patterns ↓

Multisyllabic decoding ↓

Instead of saying:

“Reading Level 3.”

Show:

WHAT THEY ACTUALLY KNOW.

Then teach:

The next skill.

🔥

⚡ FLUENCY BUILDER™

Read aloud.

AI listens—with appropriate privacy and consent.

Measures useful instructional signals such as:

Accuracy.

Pacing.

Repeated hesitation.

Expression.

Then:

“Let's try that paragraph again.”

Not:

YOU SCORED 63.

Instead:

LET'S MAKE THIS EASIER TO READ.

The National Reading Panel describes fluency as an important contributor to comprehension and found value in guided repeated oral reading with feedback. (NICHD)

🔥🔥🔥

🎙️ READ TO ME™

Student reads.

Platform follows along.

Stuck?

Wait.

Give a hint.

Still stuck?

Help decode.

Then continue.

Don't interrupt every imperfection.

Don't turn reading into:

A CONSTANT EXAM.

Make it feel like:

Someone patient is sitting beside you.

🔥

📚 JUST RIGHT™

This could be powerful.

Child loves:

Dinosaurs.

Space.

Hockey.

Horses.

Robots.

Mysteries.

But reading level doesn't match the books they want.

ReadingAndLearning finds material that is:

Appropriately challenging.

Interesting.

Age-respectful.

Then:

MOTIVATION MEETS ABILITY.

🔥🔥🔥

🚀 LEVEL ME UP™

Student reads comfortably.

Increase complexity slightly.

Vocabulary expands.

Sentences become richer.

Ideas become deeper.

Not:

Level 4 → Level 5 → Level 6 forever.

Eventually remove the training wheels.

The destination is:

REAL BOOKS.

🔥

❤️ MAKE ME WANT TO READ™

This may matter as much as another assessment.

Ask:

What do you love?

Football?

Fashion?

Minecraft?

History?

Animals?

Crime?

Cars?

Space?

Anime?

Business?

Find:

THE TEXT THAT CREATES THE READER.

The OECD has long found that students who engage broadly in reading and read for enjoyment tend to be stronger learners and performers. (OECD)

🔥🔥🔥

📖 ONE MORE PAGE™

No addictive nonsense.

No casino-style learning streaks.

Instead:

Build genuine reading momentum.

“You're 4 minutes from discovering what happens.”

or:

“You just finished your longest chapter yet.”

Make accomplishment:

THE REWARD.

🔥

🧠 DID YOU GET IT?™

Reading words isn't enough.

After a section:

“Why did the character leave?”

“What caused the experiment to fail?”

“What is the author's argument?”

Not multiple-choice every time.

Let the student:

EXPLAIN.

Then AI determines whether they actually understood.

🔥🔥🔥

❓ ASK THE BOOK™

Student highlights:

“The mitochondria generate most of the cell's usable chemical energy…”

Then asks:

“What does that actually mean?”

ReadingAndLearning explains at the student's level.

Student:

“Simpler.”

Done.

“Give me an analogy.”

Done.

“Now explain it normally again.”

Done.

That's not replacing reading.

That's:

UNLOCKING THE TEXT.

🔥

💡 WHY DOES THIS MATTER?™

Sometimes comprehension fails because students can't connect information to anything they know.

Highlight:

The French Revolution.

Ask:

WHY SHOULD I CARE?

Connect it to:

Government.

Rights.

Modern Europe.

Political institutions.

Ideas.

Then return to the text.

🔥🔥🔥

🧩 CONNECT THE DOTS™

Chapter 7 mentions something from Chapter 2.

Platform notices.

“Remember this?”

Student:

“No.”

😂

Quick refresher.

Then continue.

Now reading becomes:

CONNECTED KNOWLEDGE.

🔥

🧠 REMEMBER THIS™

Not every sentence deserves memorization.

Identify important:

Concepts.

Definitions.

Arguments.

Events.

Relationships.

Then revisit them using retrieval practice.

Tomorrow:

One question.

Next week:

Another.

Later:

Apply it.

Reading becomes:

LONG-TERM LEARNING.

🔥🔥🔥

📚 FROM READING TO KNOWLEDGE™

This is where the company gets bigger.

Read:

20 books.

45 articles.

3 textbooks.

Hundreds of notes.

Normally they disappear into:

THE GREAT DIGITAL GRAVEYARD.

😂

ReadingAndLearning builds a personal knowledge structure.

What have I learned?

What ideas connect?

What have I forgotten?

What should I revisit?

MY KNOWLEDGE™

🔥

🗺️ KNOWLEDGE MAP™

Student studies:

World War II.

Map connects:

Treaty of Versailles.

Weimar Republic.

Great Depression.

Fascism.

Appeasement.

Invasion of Poland.

Allied powers.

Holocaust.

Pacific War.

Postwar order.

Now history isn't:

97 DISCONNECTED FACTS.

It's:

A SYSTEM OF CAUSES AND CONSEQUENCES.

🔥🔥🔥

🧬 WORD DNA™

New word:

Benevolent.

Don't merely show:

adjective: well meaning and kindly.

Show:

Pronunciation.

Meaning.

Context.

Word family.

Synonyms.

Opposites.

Examples.

Then find it again later in real reading.

Eventually:

VOCABULARY BECOMES OWNED, NOT MEMORIZED.

🔥

📈 MY WORDS™

Words encountered:

4,281.

Newly understood:

Comfortably recognized:

Still developing:

But avoid turning vocabulary into vanity metrics.

The goal isn't:

COLLECTING WORDS.

It's:

UNDERSTANDING LANGUAGE.

🔥🔥🔥

📰 READ THE INTERNET™

Now move beyond school.

Article.

Blog.

News story.

Government page.

Scientific source.

Social post.

ReadingAndLearning asks:

Who wrote it?

What's the claim?

What's evidence?

What's opinion?

What's missing?

What source supports this?

This is increasingly part of literacy itself: the OECD defines modern reading literacy as understanding, evaluating and reflecting on texts, including navigating multiple digital sources and distinguishing fact from opinion. (OECD)

🔥

🕵️ SHOW ME THE CLAIM™

Article says:

“Scientists prove…”

Pause.

What scientists?

What study?

What exactly was found?

Correlation?

Causation?

Sample size?

Original source?

Teach people:

HOW TO READ CLAIMS.

Not simply:

What to believe.

🔥🔥🔥

⚖️ FACT / OPINION / ARGUMENT™

Give a passage.

Student identifies:

Fact.

Interpretation.

Opinion.

Prediction.

Argument.

Evidence.

Then explain:

WHY.

That's literacy for:

THE AI AGE.

🔥

🤖 AI SAID WHAT?™

This could become extremely relevant.

AI gives an answer.

ReadingAndLearning asks the student:

“Which claims should we verify?”

Then:

Find sources.

Compare.

Evaluate.

The OECD's September 2026 discussion of PISA findings specifically emphasizes critical evaluation of AI-generated information as literacy becomes more important—not less—in an AI-rich world. (OECD)

So don't teach children:

ASK AI.

Teach them:

READ AI CRITICALLY.

🔥🔥🔥

📄 READ ANYTHING™

Eventually:

Book.

PDF.

Website.

Essay.

Email.

Research paper.

Manual.

Contract.

News story.

Instructions.

Textbook.

ReadingAndLearning adapts its help to:

WHAT YOU'RE TRYING TO LEARN.

🔥

🔬 SCIENCE READER™

Scientific text has:

Vocabulary.

Dense sentences.

Charts.

Methods.

Claims.

Evidence.

Teach students how to:

READ SCIENCE LIKE SCIENCE.

🔥

🏛️ HISTORY READER™

Who wrote this?

When?

For whom?

Why?

What perspective?

What happened before?

What happened afterward?

Now primary sources become:

UNDERSTANDABLE.

🔥🔥🔥

➗ MATH READER™

Underrated problem:

Sometimes the student understands arithmetic.

They don't understand:

THE QUESTION.

Break down word problems.

What information matters?

What's being asked?

What relationship exists?

Don't solve immediately.

Teach the student to:

READ MATHEMATICS.

🔥

📝 STUDY MODE™

Exam Friday.

Don't create:

A 19-page AI summary.

😂

Use what the student actually read.

Generate:

Questions.

Recall prompts.

Concept connections.

Practice.

Explain-back exercises.

Then identify:

WHAT THEY DON'T YET UNDERSTAND.

🔥🔥🔥

🎓 TEACH IT BACK™

This could become one of the best features.

Student reads concept.

AI says:

“Teach it to me.”

Student explains.

AI asks:

“Why?”

Student explains again.

Then:

“Give me an example.”

If you can teach it:

YOU PROBABLY UNDERSTAND IT.

🔥

🧠 I DON'T GET IT™

One button.

No embarrassment.

No judgment.

Press:

I DON'T GET IT.

AI tries:

Simpler wording.

Different example.

Diagram.

Analogy.

Prerequisite concept.

Short video where appropriate.

Then asks:

“Better?”

Learning systems need:

MULTIPLE DOORS INTO THE SAME IDEA.

🔥🔥🔥

🧑‍🏫 TEACHER MODE™

Teacher assigns:

Chapter 4.

Dashboard doesn't merely say:

27 students opened it.

Who cares?

😂

Show:

Where comprehension broke down.

Vocabulary causing difficulty.

Concepts frequently misunderstood.

Questions students asked.

Sections reread.

Aggregate patterns with appropriate privacy.

Teacher sees:

WHAT NEEDS TEACHING TOMORROW.

🔥

📚 CLASS READING™

Teacher selects text.

Platform creates:

Before-reading knowledge activation.

Vocabulary support.

During-reading questions.

After-reading comprehension.

Discussion prompts.

Extension.

But:

TEACHER CONTROLS THE LESSON.

AI assists.

🔥🔥🔥

👨‍👩‍👧 READ TOGETHER™

Parent + child.

Choose book.

Platform suggests:

Questions.

Conversation prompts.

Vocabulary.

Fun connections.

Not:

TURN BEDTIME INTO SCHOOL.

Keep the story:

The story.

Help parents know when to:

Ask.

Explain.

Or simply:

KEEP READING.

🔥

🌙 BEDTIME LEARNING™

Read aloud.

Child asks:

“What's a constellation?”

Quick explanation.

Back to story.

No rabbit hole.

No dashboard.

No test.

Sometimes learning should feel like:

CURIOSITY.

🔥🔥🔥

🌍 LEARN A LANGUAGE BY READING™

Same platform becomes powerful for:

English.

French.

Spanish.

German.

Japanese.

Anything.

Read slightly above ability.

Tap unfamiliar phrase.

Hear pronunciation.

See contextual translation.

Save vocabulary.

Gradually reduce assistance.

Eventually:

READ WITHOUT TRANSLATION.

🔥

🗣️ BILINGUAL MODE™

Read:

French.

Need help?

Explain in English.

Then gradually shift explanations into French as proficiency increases.

This turns authentic text into:

A LANGUAGE CLASSROOM.

🔥🔥🔥

♿ READING ACCESS™

Dyslexia-friendly presentation options.

Text-to-speech.

Adjustable spacing.

Font choices.

Contrast.

Reading ruler.

Audio synchronization.

Simplified explanations where requested.

But don't claim:

ONE SETTING WORKS FOR EVERY LEARNER.

Give control.

Support accessibility.

🔥

🎧 READ + LISTEN™

Text and narration synchronized.

Useful for:

Language learners.

Developing readers.

Accessibility.

Complex texts.

Then gradually:

Audio off.

Read independently.

Support should:

BUILD INDEPENDENCE.

Not permanent dependence.

🔥🔥🔥

🚫 NO SHAME MODE™

Adult struggles with reading?

No childish graphics.

No:

“GREAT JOB, SUPERSTAR!”

😂

Give:

Adult topics.

Work documents.

News.

Financial literacy.

Everyday forms.

Professional vocabulary.

Private learning.

Respect.

Because literacy isn't:

ONLY A CHILDHOOD PRODUCT.

🔥

🧑‍🔧 READ FOR WORK™

Mechanic:

Service manual.

Nurse:

Clinical material.

Electrician:

Technical documentation.

Entrepreneur:

Contract.

Employee:

Training.

ReadingAndLearning explains terminology while preserving the original meaning and flags when professional expertise is needed.

Now:

LITERACY BECOMES WORKFORCE INFRASTRUCTURE.

🔥🔥🔥

👵 LEARN FOREVER™

History at 67.

Astronomy at 52.

Finance at 41.

Spanish at 73.

AI at 60.

ReadingAndLearning shouldn't end after graduation.

Because reading proficiency is fundamental to continuing to learn throughout life. (OECD)

The bigger category is:

LIFELONG LEARNING THROUGH READING.

🔥

🎯 WHAT DO YOU WANT TO LEARN?™

This changes onboarding completely.

Don't ask:

“What books do you like?”

Ask:

WHAT DO YOU WANT TO KNOW?

Space.

Investing.

Ancient Rome.

Psychology.

Cooking.

Artificial intelligence.

Climate.

Business.

Then construct:

Beginner reading.

Intermediate reading.

Advanced reading.

Primary sources.

Questions.

Knowledge map.

Now the platform becomes:

A SELF-DIRECTED UNIVERSITY.

🔥🔥🔥

🛤️ LEARNING PATH™

User says:

“Teach me economics.”

Don't generate:

ECONOMICS IN 10 BULLETS.

Build:

Book.

Chapter.

Essay.

Article.

Concept.

Question.

Next reading.

Review.

Application.

Over months:

ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE.

🔥

📚 HUMAN LIBRARY™

Teachers.

Authors.

Researchers.

Librarians.

Tutors.

Subject experts.

Curate:

WHAT IS WORTH READING.

AI can recommend.

Humans can curate.

Together:

Better learning paths.

🔥🔥🔥

🏫 SCHOOL LIBRARY 2.0™

Imagine every school library gaining:

Personal reading recommendations.

Reading support.

Research assistance.

Source evaluation.

Learning paths.

Teacher collections.

Librarian curation.

But without replacing:

THE LIBRARIAN.

Make librarians:

Superpowered.

🔥

📕 BOOK → COURSE™

Any suitable book can become:

Reading experience.

Questions.

Vocabulary.

Discussion.

Recall.

Projects.

Further reading.

Author content where licensed.

Expert commentary.

Now publishers can sell:

THE BOOK + THE LEARNING EXPERIENCE.

🔥🔥🔥

✍️ AUTHOR CLASSROOM™

Author writes:

Climate book.

History book.

Business book.

Children's novel.

Add:

Author explanations.

Questions.

Behind-the-book material.

Teaching guides.

Live sessions.

Readers don't just consume the work.

THEY LEARN THROUGH IT.

🔥

🏢 PUBLISHER MODE™

Publishers get:

Licensed interactive editions.

Education layers.

Classroom tools.

Reading analytics with privacy safeguards.

Course extensions.

School distribution.

Now ReadingAndLearning can become:

INFRASTRUCTURE BETWEEN PUBLISHING AND EDUCATION.

🔥🔥🔥

🔌 READING API™

This is where it gets much larger.

Any education product sends:

Text.

Student level.

Learning objective.

ReadingAndLearning returns:

Vocabulary support.

Comprehension questions.

Difficulty signals.

Concept map.

Prerequisites.

Discussion prompts.

Recall schedule.

Now:

LMS.

Tutoring platforms.

Libraries.

Publishers.

Schools.

Language apps.

AI education products.

can add:

READING INTELLIGENCE.

🔥

🧠 COMPREHENSION ENGINE™

Not merely:

“What grade level is this?”

Understand:

Sentence complexity.

Vocabulary.

Background knowledge.

Concept density.

Argument structure.

Inference demands.

Student familiarity.

Then answer:

WHY IS THIS TEXT HARD FOR THIS READER?

That's much more valuable.

🔥🔥🔥

📈 MY READING™

Don't reduce the human being to:

READING SCORE: 742

Track useful progress:

Decoding.

Fluency.

Vocabulary.

Comprehension.

Reading stamina.

Genres explored.

Concepts learned.

Confidence.

And let:

Teacher.

Student.

Parent where appropriate.

understand:

WHAT IS IMPROVING.

🔥

🔐 PRIVATE READER™

What someone reads can reveal:

Health concerns.

Religion.

Politics.

Relationships.

Finances.

Identity.

Personal problems.

So:

Reading history deserves serious privacy.

Minimize data.

Clear controls.

Private mode.

Deletion.

No creepy ad targeting.

No:

“We noticed you read about divorce…”

Absolutely not.

TRUST IS PART OF LITERACY TECHNOLOGY.

🔥🔥🔥

🤖 LEARNING AGENT™

Eventually:

“I want to understand artificial intelligence.”

Agent builds reading path.

You read.

It helps when needed.

Tests understanding.

Finds gaps.

Recommends next text.

Revisits forgotten concepts.

Connects new ideas to old ones.

Six months later:

You didn't merely:

CHAT ABOUT AI.

You:

LEARNED AI.

That's the difference.

Here's the moat.

Connect:

Reader.

Word.

Sentence.

Concept.

Book.

Article.

Author.

Subject.

Question.

Misconception.

Prerequisite.

Explanation.

Memory.

Knowledge.

Then understand:

Which text teaches which concept?

What background knowledge does it require?

Which vocabulary blocks comprehension?

Which explanation unlocks it?

What should the reader read next?

Eventually:

THE PLATFORM UNDERSTANDS HOW READING BECOMES KNOWLEDGE.

Because these aren't two unrelated words.

They describe:

CAUSE → EFFECT.

Reading

creates access to

Learning.

And the name isn't trapped inside:

Children.

Schools.

Books.

Tutoring.

Phonics.

It can span:

A 5-year-old decoding a first sentence.

A 15-year-old understanding history.

THE BUYER PITCH

AI can write.

AI can summarize.

AI can answer.

AI can explain.

But there's a dangerous possibility:

THE BETTER MACHINES GET AT READING FOR US…

THE LESS WE PRACTICE READING FOR OURSELVES.

And reading isn't merely how we consume words.

It's how we:

Build vocabulary.

Acquire knowledge.

Follow arguments.

Encounter ideas.

Evaluate evidence.

Develop imagination.

Learn independently.

So don't build another product that helps people:

SKIP THE BOOK.

Build the platform that makes them:

BETTER READERS.

Because once someone can read deeply…

They can teach themselves:

ALMOST ANYTHING.

Cohen and AARON: the long AI projectHarold Cohen, already a painter who had represented Britain at Venice, starts AARON in the early 1970s after time at Stanford’s AI Lab. It is not a prompt box. It is a drawing program he rewrites for decades: first abstract marks, then plants and figures, then color. AARON draws; Cohen designs what AARON is allowed to know about composition, closure, and form. Museums let it work in public at SFMOMA and the Tate. That is still the cleanest historical example of an artist building a collaborator instead of renting a generator.

1980s–1990s: fractals, scenes, closed shopsMandelbrot’s fractals leak into popular “computer art.” Plotter and algorithmic artists keep working with less fashion heat. The demoscene treats realtime code as craft. John Maeda’s Design By Numbers at MIT tries to give visual people a programming language small enough to sketch with. Flash becomes a mass tool for motion systems. The through-line is the same: code as pencil, not code as vending machine.2001: ProcessingCasey Reas and Ben Fry release Processing, built out of Maeda’s MIT orbit. Goal: artists and designers write systems the way they used to sketch. Reas’s own Process series is explicit LeWitt-into-software: rules for elements and behaviors, then the program runs. Jared Tarbell, Marius Watz, and a generation of “creative coders” come out of that stack. Open source matters here. The tool is inspectable. The system can be shown, not only the JPEG.

AI IS NOT THE ENEMY

I am profoundly tired of hearing people call artificial intelligence evil.

AI is accelerating medical research, processing information at enormous scale, and giving ordinary people capabilities once reserved for wealthy institutions. Work that took weeks can now begin in seconds. That does not make human intelligence irrelevant. It gives it greater reach.

If you hate AI that much, get off your phone because you already use it all day, every day. Turn off Face ID, autocorrect, predictive text, voice assistants, camera enhancements, translation, navigation, spam filters, fraud protection, banking security, and recommendations. Shut down YouTube and social media. Stop shopping online or in stores using AI for inventory, security, and fraud prevention. Give up streaming, delivery, rideshare, and smart devices too.

You do not hate AI. You hate the AI you can see while benefiting from the AI you cannot.

That does not make every use acceptable. Data centers are a legitimate concern, and I oppose massive facilities wherever they would strain water, electricity, land, infrastructure, or residents’ quality of life. Build responsibly, protect communities, demand transparency, and make corporations pay their fair share. Opposing irresponsible development is not opposing AI.

If someone uses AI to deceive, fabricate reality, destroy reputations, or manipulate people, blame the person who made that choice. The problem is not AI. The problem is the user.

If a student submits an AI-generated thesis without reading the research, examining the evidence, or thinking independently, that is intellectual laziness and academic dishonesty. Use AI to find studies and compare arguments. Then read, investigate, question, and think for yourself. AI should expand your mind, not replace it.

AI may beat us in speed, scale, and pattern recognition, but it has no conscience, faith, lived experience, or moral judgment. Human beings provide purpose and understand consequences.

And please spare me the moral outrage every time someone creates an image or film with AI.

I am an artist. Before Photoshop or any digital tool, I painted with brushes and my own hands. I still paint today. Then I learned Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Lightroom, Procreate, Premiere Pro, After Effects, Canva, and CapCut. Every one expanded what I could create without taking away the imagination or ability behind it. AI is simply the next tool in that evolution.

What do people expect me to do, paint every pixel by hand with a tiny brush before my work is legitimate? Get the fuck out of here with that. AI helps bring a human vision to life. It does not create that vision by itself.

Look at @NemPerez’s extraordinary five-minute film, the $100,000 grand prize winner of the Grok Imagine x Homer’s Odyssey Contest. Grok did not conceive its vision, shape its emotion, direct its scenes, or refine the finished work by itself.

Grok supplied the capability. The artist supplied the vision. The result was unbelievable. (Attached below)

We can discuss copyright, consent, and protecting artists without attacking everyone who uses AI. Creativity does not belong exclusively to people using the tools you approve of. You do not want to use AI? Don’t. That is your prerogative.

And let’s be honest, many of the loudest people sneering at AI creators do not have a damn thing of their own to show. They create nothing, risk nothing, and build nothing, yet feel entitled to police the people doing the work. Critics complain while creators create.

You create your way and I will create mine, so don’t tread on me and I won’t tread on you. Got it?

The future is not humans against AI. It is thoughtful humans working with AI to accomplish things neither could alone. Human intelligence created this technology, human wisdom must guide it, and fear will not stop what is coming.
